title: Pope Leo XIV Will Open a Giant Tower and Meet Migrants in Spain
summary: Have you ever seen pictures of the Sagrada Familia in Barcelona? It's a giant, amazing church that's been under construction for over 140 years! In June, Pope Leo XIV will visit to open its tallest tower—the Tower of Jesus Christ. At 172.5 meters, that's about as tall as a 50-story building! The tower was put in place in February, but the church still isn't finished. The pope's trip isn't just about the tower. He'll also go to the Canary Islands, near Africa, to meet migrants. Many people from Africa travel there in small boats, hoping for a better life in Europe. Last year, nearly 47,000 arrived! The pope wants to show kindness to them, just like Pope Francis did before him. In Madrid, Leo will meet Spain's king and queen and even speak to the parliament—a rare honor. He'll also pray with young people, remembering the last papal visit in 2011. The trip happens around the 100th anniversary of the death of Antoni Gaudí, the architect who designed Sagrada Familia. He might become a saint one day, but not during this visit. From a sky-high tower to meeting migrants, this trip is full of history and heart.
why_it_matters: This story shows how faith and kindness can inspire people to both celebrate amazing human creations like the Sagrada Familia and care for those in need, no matter where they come from.

background_read: The Sagrada Familia is a one-of-a-kind church in Barcelona, Spain, designed by Antoni Gaudí (a creative architect who died in 1926). Construction began in 1882 and is still not finished. Pope Leo XIV (head of the Catholic Church since 2024) follows the example of Pope Francis, who often reached out to the poor and migrants. The Canary Islands, a group of Spanish islands near Africa, have become a main arrival point for thousands of African migrants risking their lives in small boats.
Article_Structure: WHO: Pope Leo XIV, the leader of the Catholic Church.
WHAT: He will open the Tower of Jesus Christ at Sagrada Familia and visit migrants in the Canary Islands.
WHERE: Barcelona for the church opening, and the Canary Islands to meet migrants.
WHY: To mark a major moment for the iconic church and to show care for people seeking a better life.

perspectives.description: Many Catholics and architecture lovers are excited about the completion of a stunning tower, a symbol of human creativity and faith.
Advocates for migrants applaud the pope for drawing attention to the struggles of people fleeing hardship, showing the Church's social mission.
The visit connects the long-planned church to the memory of its architect Antoni Gaudí, linking past and present through a single event.
